newsitem.title: CANADA: ConAgra to build three Canadian elevators.
newsitem.headline: ConAgra to build three Canadian elevators.

text.p: ConAgra Grain, Canada will build three grain elevators in Saskatchewan at a cost of more than C$30 million, a company statement released Thursday said.

Construction of the high throughput terminals at Corinne, Nokomis and Yorkton, Saskatchewan, should be complete by next summer, said Mayo Schmidt, president of the Canadian division of the U.S.-based ConAgra Inc, a multinational food processor.
"We intend to be handling grain by next harvest," he said.
There were 1,333 licensed, primary elevators on Canada's Prairies as of July 31, 1995, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
Canadian grain handlers have closed some since then.
The industry has been replacing low capacity, wooden elevators with larger, concrete terminals that can load more hopper cars at a time and faster, thereby expediting turnover.
Schmidt was not immediately available for comment.
Each ConAgra facility will be able to load a 100-hopper car train within eight hours. The steel structures will feature bulk handling capability, condominium-type storage as well as retail services.
The terminals should handle 30 million bushels (1.1 million cubic metres).
The announcement marks the second phase of the firm's investment strategy in Canada.

Other ConAgra holdings in Canada include barley maltster Canada Malting Co Ltd CMG.TO, flour miller Maple Leaf Mills and oat processor Westglen Milling. Also, construction has begun on its Alberta BioClean fuels plant.
